_comment: Tool policy for spec-critic.sh: the fresh, read-only `claude -p` pass that
attacks a brief before anything downstream treats it as ground truth.
The brief is UNTRUSTED TEXT. A self-briefed one is written from a Linear
description any workspace member can edit, and a hand-written one is quoted
into this prompt the same way. A critic with a shell is a critic a brief can
turn into a shell — permission patterns match the head of a command line and
cannot see what it goes on to execute or redirect — so there is no Bash rule
in allow at all and Bash is denied besides. Task goes with it: a subagent is
a second context with a turn budget of its own, reading the same brief with
none of this caller's suspicion.
A critic that can write is a critic that can edit the brief it is grading.
Edit and Write are denied outright: the verdict leaves through the CLI's
--json-schema structured output, and nothing else in this stage needs a
file. spec-critic.sh gives the session a disposable scratch dir as its cwd
and --add-dir's the repo it may research, so the write confinement holds
even if a future release relaxes one of these rules.
Read, Grep and Glob are what it needs and all it gets: evidence for a
conflict has to be a file:line in the target repo, which is exactly what
those three can produce. The network tools are denied so the brief cannot
leave the machine, and the harness's own secrets are denied by path — a
critic that can read them writes them into a verdict later stages quote.
